Benchmarking cloud detectors

Source: vignettes/benchmarking.Rmd
benchmarking.Rmd

Why simulate at all

Hand-labelled benchmarks have a ceiling. Annotators disagree at thin-cloud boundaries, shadow is the weakest-labelled class in every published dataset, and the scenes chosen for labelling are rarely the surfaces where masks actually fail. Simulation is complementary, not a replacement: truth is exact, and difficulty is a dial rather than a property of whichever scenes someone labelled.

A controlled scene 

bg <- list(blue = matrix(0.06, 128, 128), green = matrix(0.08, 128, 128),
           red = matrix(0.05, 128, 128), nir = matrix(0.32, 128, 128),
           swir16 = matrix(0.20, 128, 128), swir22 = matrix(0.12, 128, 128))

sim <- cl_simulate(background = bg, coverage = 0.28, opacity = c(0.35, 1),
                   height = 2200, res = 30, sun_zenith = 42,
                   sun_azimuth = 155, seed = 7)
c(realised_coverage = round(mean(sim$cloud), 3),
  shadow_pixels = sum(sim$shadow))
#> realised_coverage     shadow_pixels 
#>              0.28           2093.00

Opacity is the difficulty control. Fully opaque cloud is easy for every method; methods separate between roughly 0.2 and 0.6, which is where thin cirrus and cloud edges live and where published masks disagree most.

Comparing methods, with uncertainty 

m_thr <- cl_probability(sim$bands, "threshold", sensor = "sentinel-2-msi")
m_fm  <- cl_probability(sim$bands, "fmask",     sensor = "sentinel-2-msi")

cmp <- cl_compare(list(threshold = m_thr$class, fmask = m_fm$class),
                  sim$cloud, n_boot = 300)
cmp$summary
#>      method  accuracy     lower     upper
#> 2     fmask 0.9862671 0.9849413 0.9874345
#> 1 threshold 0.9191284 0.9161298 0.9221349
cmp$pairwise[, c("method_a", "method_b", "mcnemar_chi2", "p_value")]
#>    method_a method_b mcnemar_chi2       p_value
#> 1 threshold    fmask     1098.001 8.982063e-241

A ranking without an interval is not a result. Two methods differing by a few tenths of a percent on one scene are not distinguishable, and McNemar’s test on the paired outcomes is the right instrument because the same pixels are scored by both.

For spatially autocorrelated masks a pixel-wise bootstrap understates uncertainty. Pass block = with tile identifiers for an honest interval.

Discrimination is not calibration 

c(auc   = round(attr(cl_roc(m_fm$probability, sim$cloud), "auc"), 3),
  brier = round(attr(cl_calibration(m_fm$probability, sim$cloud), "brier"), 4),
  ece   = round(attr(cl_calibration(m_fm$probability, sim$cloud), "ece"), 4))
#>    auc  brier    ece 
#> 1.0000 0.0199 0.0935

A method can rank pixels perfectly and still emit probabilities that mean nothing, in which case they cannot be used to weight observations or propagate uncertainty. Reporting AUC alone hides this. During development of this package, an early Fmask implementation scored AUC 1.000 with expected calibration error 0.373 — the ranking was perfect and the threshold was in entirely the wrong place. The calibration diagnostic caught it; accuracy at the default threshold was 0.61.

Disagreement without labels 

cl_disagreement(list(threshold = m_thr$class, fmask = m_fm$class))$pairwise
#>    method_a method_b agreement   jaccard a_only     b_only   cloud_a   cloud_b
#> 1 threshold    fmask 0.9328613 0.7478799      0 0.06713867 0.1991577 0.2662964

This needs no reference labels at all, which is what makes it deployable globally. Passing strata = — a land-cover or snow layer — reports where methods diverge, and those are the regions where a derived cloud statistic should carry a caveat.

A difficulty gradient 

bench <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0), function(op) {
  s <- cl_simulate(background = bg, coverage = 0.3, opacity = op, seed = 21)
  m <- cl_probability(s$bands, "fmask", sensor = "sentinel-2-msi")
  v <- cl_validate(m$class, s$cloud)
  i <- which(v$class == "1")
  data.frame(opacity = op, recall = round(v$recall[i], 3),
             precision = round(v$precision[i], 3), iou = round(v$iou[i], 3))
}))
bench
#>   opacity recall precision   iou
#> 1    0.15  0.355         1 0.355
#> 2    0.30  0.712         1 0.712
#> 3    0.50  0.843         1 0.843
#> 4    0.80  1.000         1 1.000
#> 5    1.00  1.000         1 1.000

Reporting a single accuracy number for a cloud detector conceals exactly this curve. Two methods with identical overall accuracy can behave completely differently on thin cloud, which is where most of the disagreement in operational products lives.

Using real benchmarks 

cl_benchmark("cloudsen12", n = 50)

Benchmark imagery ships in the companion data package. cl_benchmark("synthetic") generates scenes on the fly and needs nothing.
